sentences.text: The animal belongs to the genus Deinocheirus, with the only known species being Deinocheirus mirificus.
It was the largest ornithomimosaur, reaching 11 meters in length and weighing 6.5 tons.
Tall neural spines on its vertebrae formed a sail-like structure along its back.
The skull measured 1.024 meters long, featuring a wide bill and a deep lower jaw similar to those of hadrosaurs.
Osmólska and Roniewicz named the genus in 1970 after the first remains were found by Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska on July 9, 1965, in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
Two additional complete specimens were described in 2014.
Deinocheirus is thought to have been omnivorous, with evidence including plant indicators, fish scales, and gastroliths.
Unlike other ornithomimosaurians, deinocheirids were not built for running; researchers suggest Deinocheirus used its long arms and blunt claws for digging and gathering plants.
The blunt claws on Deinocheirus's feet may have prevented it from sinking into the substrate while wading.
Deinocheirus is classified as a primitive ornithomimosaurian closely related to Garudimimus and Beishanlong, forming the family Deinocheiridae.
Osmólska and Roniewicz initially classified Deinocheirus in the new monotypic family Deinocheiridae within the infraorder Carnosauria.
Deinocheirus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
It is proposed that bite marks from Tarbosaurus caused the scattered state of the holotype specimen.
It is debated whether large tridactyl tracks found in the Nemegt locality were made by Deinocheirus, despite similarities to hadrosaur tracks and the lack of hadrosaur hand tracks.
While some writers supported a relationship between Deinocheirus and therizinosaurs, modern analysis does not consider them closely related.
The function of pneumatization in non-avian dinosaurs like Deinocheirus is not known with certainty, though it is advantageous for flight in modern birds.
